episodes.title: DARVO & Family Court: How Defending Yourself Gets You Labeled "High Conflict"
episodes.description:
Navigating family court can feel overwhelming, dizzying, and deeply unfair. In this episode, we break down DARVO (Deny, Attack, Reverse Victim and Offender)—one of the most common manipulation tactics used in high-conflict custody disputes and co-parenting.
Through real-life examples from our own custody cases, we discuss how false allegations can swiftly shift the focus away from the original bad behavior and onto the parent who is simply trying to protect themselves or their children.
We dive deep into how accusations of "parental alienation," mental instability, and being "high-conflict" are often weaponized against protective parents, and how the legal system—from custody evaluations to aggressive litigation tactics—can accidentally escalate the chaos.
🔍 What We Cover in This Episode:
The DARVO Breakdown: Exactly what Deny, Attack, and Reverse Victim & Offender looks like in practice.
The Courtroom Weapon: How DARVO manifests in family court, custody litigation strategy, and motions to compel.
The "High-Conflict" Label: Why parents are frequently labeled "high-conflict" just for defending themselves.
Systemic Traps: The roles of Guardian ad Litems (GALs), mental health evaluations, and attorney ethics in custody disputes.
Survival & Reform: Dealing with gaslighting, writing better parenting plans, and the urgent need for family court reform.
Whether you are currently in the middle of a brutal custody battle, trying to draft a bulletproof parenting plan, or just trying to make sense of a high-conflict ex, this episode will help you name the tactics being used against you so you can navigate the system more effectively.
